a couple days late on the recap from last week:
The first Breakfast Club SOMa of 2026 was everything. A great crew of regulars, friends, and some newcomers took over our usual table (and a few additional spots) at Artie's.
We talked about some of the heavy stuff happening in the world, about the world of work, about networking. But mostly we talked about broken prosthetics, Florida Man, manifesting good things with totems of good luck, the power of story, christian nationalist psychos, conspiracies, losing friends, making friends, being unemployable, the Workday class action lawsuit for AI age discrimination, ageism more broadly, revolving leaders and their stables of go-tos, the evolving market for different styles of antiques, getting ghosted on Marketplace, foot fetishists, ski accidents, Marty Supreme, going to the movies, the Good Wife and the Good Fight, Slow Horses, how do tchotchke stores stay in business? and the dreaded meat sleeps.

Here’s my ChatGPT 🙄recap of our first BC of the year in Milan  …..
Breakfast Club Milan
Recap, Friday Edition
Our first Breakfast Club of 2026 took place in a cool new art gallery that had opened its doors only the day before. The space gave the morning a fresh, intimate energy. The artist was present, which made the experience even more special. Guests were taken through the full body of work and the conceptual narrative behind each piece, sparking a lot of curiosity and conversation.
After the tour, everyone settled in with coffee, croissants, and very lively discussions. A few themes surfaced throughout the morning:
Cultural and Global Pulse
• The Olympics and the noticeable lack of enthusiasm from the Milanese.
• ICE presence in Italy and the wider geopolitical mood.
• The ongoing chaos of US politics, especially the latest Donald Trump conversations.
Work, Creativity, and Industry Realities
• Brand collaborations, Design Week, and Fashion Week planning.
• People leaving jobs, being made redundant, and what that means for personal reinvention.
• The big question of whether the job market will truly open up in 2026.
• How connections formed at brands like Diesel have a way of resurfacing and bringing people back together.
• Presentation and Excel skills becoming rare among the new generation. This one got a lot of laughs and nods of agreement.
Community and What’s Next
We wrapped by talking about the next Breakfast Club Milan location and timing. Everyone is looking forward to the February edition. There is also early momentum around hosting a second format, an evening version of Breakfast Club, in the coming months.
A smaller turnout than hoped for, but the conversations were rich, personal, and exactly why this community exists. Looking forward to the next one. Let’s keep building this space for curiosity, creativity, and connection.
